description: Baseline: default architecture, random init; also logs the task's public interface.
First e01 attempt: assert failed because the pattern thought_provoking exceeds the 16-char window; stopped before eval.
Char-window attention, one AND neuron per hand-written lexicon pattern (weights +-1,+-2), summed sentiment at '='; ties positive.
e01 minus the function words no/not/never/only/yet/however as negative evidence, ahead of real negation handling.
e01 plus a -1 suffix pattern *less that fires on any word ending in -less (pointless, witless, listless).
e03 plus about 50 more hand-written patterns: warmth and craft words (+1), hedging and cliche words (-1).
e04 with the threshold moved so zero-score phrases are called negative instead of positive.
e04 plus a negation circuit: offset heads count negators in the previous 15 chars, gated ReLUs flip SCORE (positive to -1x, negative to +0.5x).
e06 with implicit negators nothing, lack*, little and less added to the set that flips nearby scores.
e07 plus about 220 hand-written critic-vocabulary patterns of both polarities; mean* narrowed to whole-word mean.
e08 with negation scope cut from 15 characters to 8, about one following word.
e09 with negated negative words flipped at full strength (+1x instead of +0.5x).
e10 with the threshold shifted to +1.5 so one mild negative word alone no longer decides a phrase.
e10 plus a contrast circuit: a uniform head records any earlier but/however/though/although/yet, and gated ReLUs double every score after it.
First e13 attempt: assert failed because the pattern straight_to_video exceeds the 16-char window; stopped before eval.
e10 (contrast circuit removed, it added nothing) plus about 100 more hand-written patterns, including common words like just, even and worse.
e13 plus intensifier bigram patterns (very good, so funny, really good) as extra evidence on top of the unigram. BUG: very_bad* and so_bad* were placed in the +2 tier by mistake; fixed in e15.
e14 with the polarity bug fixed: very_bad* and so_bad* moved to the -2 tier.
e13 (intensifier bigrams removed, they added nothing) with the broad positive tier weakened from +1 to +0.75.
e13 with the mild negative tier strengthened from -1 to -1.5 and the positive tier restored to +1.
e13 with the character window cut from 16 to 14, shrinking width and head count; five long patterns shortened to fit.
e18 plus about 80 hand-written patterns for review phrasing: craft praise, adverbs, and hedges like would_be and ultimately.
e19 minus words that appear in reviews of either polarity: performance, acting, direction, oscar, ultimately, almost and similar.
e20 minus the modal-phrase patterns would_be, could_have, want_to and similar, which can appear in positive phrases.
Ablation of e21: empty negator list, so the flip circuit never fires. Measures what negation contributes with the larger vocabulary.
e22 with the unused negation circuit deleted: two blocks only, one reads words and one pools sentiment.
Ablation of e23: strength tiers collapsed, every pattern scores exactly +1 or -1.
e23 (tiers restored) with the pooling block reduced to one head of width 1, removing about 1M unused zero weights.
e25 with separate key and value widths: 3-dim position keys and 32-dim character values, shrinking the attention matrices.
Lexicon audit of e26: removes near-neutral negatives only, yet, however, dark, long and familiar.
Lexicon audit of e27: removes the *less suffix pattern, which also fires on less, unless and nevertheless.
Lexicon audit of e28: removes broad positive stems well, pretty, real, true, family, heart*, soul*, human*, emotion*, visual*.
Lexicon audit of e29: removes common words just, any, anything, even, mostly, enough, minutes and rather from the negative tier.
Lexicon audit of e30: removes descriptive non-judgement words comic*, comedy, tense*, tight*, slick*, complex*, tears*, cry*, quietly*, intensely*.
e31 with the explicit negators no, not, never, n't and nothing promoted from the -1 tier to -2.
e32 with too, lack* and without also promoted from the -1 tier to -2.
e33 plus negative multi-word idioms: at best, fails to, falls short, not very, little more and similar. Includes a dead pattern than_a_ that can never fire; removed in e35.
e34 (dead pattern than_a_ removed) plus positive idioms: a must, a joy, of the year, not bad, never dull and similar.
e35 with double-negative idioms (not bad, never dull) moved to a +5 tier so they outweigh their own negative parts.
e33 lexicon (idioms removed, they added nothing) with a 12-character window; over-long patterns now truncate to a prefix automatically.
e37 with a 10-character window: longer patterns match their first nine characters as a prefix.
e38 with an 8-character window: longer patterns match their first seven characters as a prefix.
e39 with a 6-character window: longer patterns match their first five characters as a prefix.
e40 with a 7-character window, locating the smallest window between the 6 that lost accuracy and the 8 that did not.
e39 window of 8 with a tight channel layout: 8 x 32 character dims plus 5 control dims, instead of slots padded to width 35.
e42 with one virtual leading space instead of KW; heads reaching before the text land on that space, a valid word boundary.
e43 with positive-side overlapping and duplicate lexicon entries removed. Corrected description: negative-side overlaps remained until e45, so words could still double-count here.
e44 with the negative-side overlaps removed too (fail*/fails, pain*/painful*, mess*/messy, hate*/hated and similar).
e45 with the never-used head 0 removed: exactly seven heads, one per character offset 1 to 7.
e46 with attention sharpness BETA lowered from 30 to 8, so the circuit does not rely on extreme weights.
